title: Human Index photographic portfolio layout
intent: Photography and public interfaces make situated work credible while remaining public-safe, accessible, project-specific, and subordinate to human publication authority.

criteria.criterion: Every public photograph is registered once with stable dimensions, alt text, caption, credit, placement, status, permission, and interpretation boundary.

The launch candidate uses exactly five reviewed photographs: the unchanged East River hero, the Shoestring Press and Market Hotel evidence sequence, the Sunday Dinner cover, and the KC Town Hall cover.
Public assets and source code contain no EXIF payload, private archive UUID, original camera filename, People metadata, GPS data, or protected filesystem path.
The homepage photograph remains unchanged; the Fair Rent sequence retains facilitation, shared public infrastructure, and collective public action; About and Colophon remain text-led.
Every work item has one project-bound cover: Harry J. Epstein, CallNYC, and WOW List use their own public surfaces; Fair Rent NYC, Sunday Dinner, and KC Town Hall use governed photographs.
Every tag-shaped control is a keyboard-reachable link to a visible filtered work-index state, with a clear route back to the complete index.
The Human Index palette is active and gradients, decorative orbs, and bokeh are absent.
Images use Next Image, explicit intrinsic dimensions or fill, stable aspect ratios, responsive sizes, and a viewport-bounded hero.
Reviewed local image derivatives bypass runtime optimization on the single-CPU Dokku app and remain small enough for direct delivery.
Design and Knowledge Wiki records state that automated scores and staging review do not replace rights, dignity, attribution, exact-candidate production approval, or indexing approval.
